$doc: Vyomi capability registry — GCP IAM & Admin. See aws/s3.json for the contract. GCP/Azure claims have no AWS-wire probe — they are proven by 'tests' (conformance files run against the in-process router).

gcp.iam-admin.project-iam-bindings.title: IAM policy bindings (Allow tab — grant/remove access)

gcp.iam-admin.recommendations-history.title: Recommendations history
limitations: Vyomi logs applied IAM policy changes (grants and removals) here; it does not run GCP's IAM Recommender to generate new suggestions on its own, so nothing appears until you grant or remove access.

gcp.iam-admin.service-account-keys.title: Service account keys
limitations: Key creation, listing and deletion are real and stateful, but the private key material is synthetic — it cannot be used to authenticate against anything outside Vyomi.

gcp.iam-admin.service-account-metrics-lo.title: Service account Metrics tab
limitations: Shows a real series derived from the credentials this service account actually issued (access tokens, ID tokens, signed blobs/JWTs via iamcredentials.googleapis.com) — total request count, a breakdown by method and a per-day series — not Cloud Monitoring's full request/error/latency metrics (Vyomi has no request-latency telemetry pipeline).

gcp.iam-admin.service-account-logs.title: Service account Logs tab
limitations: Shows the admin-activity events Vyomi itself records for this service account — key create/delete, enable/disable, display-name updates, and Principals-with-access grants/revokes — not GCP's full Cloud Audit Log trail (e.g. API calls made using the account's own credentials).

gcp.iam-admin.audit-logs-config.title: Data Access audit logs configuration
limitations: Admin Read toggles for iam.googleapis.com are enforced: when enabled, reading service accounts, keys, custom roles or the project's IAM policy writes a real Cloud Logging entry (readable back via entries:list, e.g. the gcp-logs console); disabled writes none. Data Read / Data Write toggles are stored and returned but produce no entries for iam.googleapis.com — this service has no data-plane payload to audit (same as real GCP; mutations are Admin Activity, always written and not configurable). Toggles for every other listed service (storage, pubsub, …) are stored only — gating those services' own operations is outside this service's scope.

gcp.iam-admin.organization-policies.title: Organization policy constraints
limitations: Two predefined boolean constraints are enforced for real on both substrates: constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountCreation blocks serviceAccounts.create, and constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation blocks serviceAccounts.keys.create, whenever a policy with rules[0].enforce=true exists on the project (create one from 'Enforce predefined constraint' on this page). Every other predefined or custom constraint is created, listed and deleted for real but not evaluated against calls.

gcp.iam-admin.privileged-access-manager.title: Privileged Access Manager — Entitlements, Grants & Approve grants

gcp.iam-admin.pam-audit-logs.title: PAM Audit Logs
limitations: Shows the grant lifecycle events (requested, approved, denied, activated, expired, revoked) Vyomi's PAM core records; it does not aggregate the full Cloud Audit Log trail for entitlement changes made outside PAM.

gcp.iam-admin.pam-settings.title: PAM Settings
limitations: Notification channels and a 'require justification' default are stored per project and ENFORCED: when 'require justification' is on, grant requests submitted without one are rejected, and every grant lifecycle event (requested, activated, denied, revoked, expired) records which configured channels Vyomi would notify. Vyomi does not deliver a real email or Pub/Sub message to those channels.

gcp.iam-admin.policy-analyzer.title: Policy Analyzer
limitations: Queries who has a given role on the project from the stored IAM policy. Vyomi does not run full Cloud Asset Inventory analysis (inherited org/folder policy, resource-level IAM across products).

gcp.iam-admin.workload-identity-federati.title: Workload Identity Federation — pool creation
limitations: Creating and listing a workload identity pool is real and stateful. Connecting an external OIDC/SAML identity provider and exchanging its tokens for Google credentials is not modeled.

gcp.iam-admin.workforce-identity-federat.title: Workforce Identity Federation
limitations: Every Vyomi project has a real backing organization (core/gcp_resourcemanager_core.py's default organization); creating, listing and deleting a workforce pool under it is real and stateful. Connecting an external OIDC/SAML workforce identity provider and exchanging its tokens for Google credentials is not modeled (same limitation as the project-scoped Workload Identity Federation pools).

gcp.iam-admin.groups.title: Groups
limitations: Cloud Identity group create/get/list/delete and membership add/list/remove, under the project's real backing organization, are real and stateful. Google Workspace/Cloud Identity directory sync, group-based Gmail/Calendar resources and dynamic group membership rules are not modeled.

gcp.iam-admin.principal-access-boundary.title: Principal Access Boundary
limitations: Policies and bindings, under the project's real backing organization, are real and stateful, and ENFORCED: core/gcp_iam_core.py's testIamPermissions narrows a bound principal's access to only the resources named in its boundary's rules, even when a normal Allow-policy binding would otherwise grant more. Resource-type boundaries (vs. exact resource names) and the Boundary conditions CEL language aren't evaluated.

gcp.iam-admin.managed-workload-identitie.title: Managed Workload Identities
limitations: Managed identities nested under a workload identity pool are real and stateful — create, list, delete and certificate rotation all work, each issuing a new certificate record (serial number, notBefore/notAfter) on rotation. The certificate material is synthetic (not issued by a real CA), so it cannot be used to authenticate against anything outside Vyomi, and automatic background rotation on expiry is not modeled — rotation is explicit (same caveat as service-account keys).

gcp.iam-admin.asset-inventory.title: Asset Inventory
limitations: searchAllResources indexes what Vyomi's IAM & Resource Manager cores actually model for this project — service accounts, custom roles, workload identity pools, the project itself and its tag keys — live, from current state. It does not index resources from other GCP services (storage buckets, Pub/Sub topics, …) or keep Cloud Asset Inventory's change-history feed.

gcp.iam-admin.security-insights.title: Security Insights
limitations: A small set of real IAM-lint rules are evaluated live against the project's actual policy bindings, service-account keys and issued credentials on every call (basic-role grants, service accounts with user-managed keys, service accounts that have never issued a credential and have no keys) — not GCP's full IAM Recommender rule catalog, and findings aren't persisted or tracked for dismissal across calls.

gcp.iam-admin.quotas-system-limits.title: Quotas & System Limits
limitations: Shows real current usage (service accounts, their keys, custom roles, workload identity pools, organization policy constraints) against GCP's documented default per-project limits. Request-rate quotas (e.g. IAM API requests per minute) aren't shown — Vyomi doesn't meter API traffic — and limits are reference values only: Vyomi does not enforce them, so creating past a shown limit still succeeds.

gcp.iam-admin.identity-organization.title: Identity & Organization
limitations: Shows the project's real backing organization (display name, directory customer ID, state) via Resource Manager's project.parent -> organization lookup. Claiming domain ownership via a DNS TXT record and signing up for Google Workspace/Cloud Identity (the real console's setup flow when a project has no organization yet) aren't modeled — every Vyomi project already has one.

gcp.iam-admin.privacy-security.title: Privacy & Security
limitations: This feature requires an organization; Vyomi's GCP lens is project-scoped.

gcp.iam-admin.identity-aware-proxy.title: Identity-Aware Proxy
limitations: Per-resource IAP enable/disable and its IAM policy (roles/iap.httpsResourceAccessor) are real and stateful, and the Allow decision is ENFORCED: a checkAccess call returns the same allow/deny IAP's own proxy would — denied while IAP is off, denied without the accessor role, allowed with it. Vyomi does not run an actual HTTPS reverse proxy in front of a real backend service/App Engine app; checkAccess is the decision, not a live request path.
